property_summary: After Collect() is called, the MinSum state variable remains unchanged if initialized is true.
After a Collect call that succeeds (does not revert), the MinSum state variable should be the same as before the call.
After a successful call to Collect(uint256) that does not revert, the MinSum value is unchanged if Initialized() has been called.
After calling Initialized(), subsequent calls to Collect(uint256) should not change MinSum, regardless of fuzz parameters.
After Initialized() is called, the MinSum state variable is never changed by any subsequent call to Collect(uint256).
For any caller, after a Collect call with an amount, the MinSum state variable is never changed.
After any call to Collect, the MinSum state variable remains unchanged.
After a Collect call, the MinSum state variable is unchanged regardless of the caller or amount.
After any Collect call (reverting or not), the MinSum state variable remains unchanged.
After any Collect call (whether it succeeds or fails), the MinSum state variable always equals the original value set during setup.

After calling Collect, MinSum remains equal to its initial value (0) if initialized is false, or unchanged if initialized is true; the reference maintains MinSum as set by SetMinSum, while the mutant sets it to 0.
After Collect() reverts because acc.balance < MinSum, MinSum retains its original value set by SetMinSum, not zero.
After Collect() finishes (whether it succeeds or reverts), MinSum remains equal to the value set by SetMinSum, which is the first fuzz parameter.
After any call to Collect, MinSum must equal the value set by SetMinSum, which is the minimum of the fuzz input and a bounded value.
After a Collect call, the MinSum state variable remains unchanged from its initial value.
After a Collect call that reverts, MinSum stays unchanged from its initial value set in SetMinSum.
After any call to Collect, the value of MinSum is equal to its value after the last call to SetMinSum, even if the Collect call reverts.
After any call to Collect that succeeds, the value of MinSum remains equal to its value set by the most recent successful SetMinSum call.
After a Collect call, the value of MinSum is never greater than the value set by the last SetMinSum call.
After any successful Collect call, the value of LogFile must be set (non-zero address) if it was previously set.
After any call to Collect, the state variable LogFile must remain unchanged if the call does not revert.
After a successful Collect call, the MinSum state variable must remain unchanged
After any call to Collect, the MinSum state variable must remain unchanged (it is only set before initialization).
After any call to Collect, the stored LogFile address must equal the MinSum state variable.
After a call to Collect, the unlockTime should always be at least block.timestamp + _lockTime for the caller if the caller's balance is at least MinSum.
After a Collect call, the caller's unlockTime must be at least the sum of block.timestamp and the _lockTime from the last Put call that increased it.
The unlockTime of a caller after a Put call with a given _lockTime should be at least block.timestamp + _lockTime when the Put call increases the balance.

After a Collect call completes, if the caller's balance is at least MinSum and the call did not revert, then the caller's unlockTime must be at least the block.timestamp at the time of the last Put call that set it.

After a call to Collect, if msg.sender.balance is at least MinSum and Collect did not revert, then the caller's unlockTime (read from Acc) must be greater than block.timestamp (the time when the Collect call was made).

After Collect(_am) returns without reverting, the caller's balance in Acc is always less than or equal to the sum of all caller's previous Put values (minus collected amounts) across both versions, but in the reference the unlockTime after Put ensures Collect can only proceed after the lock expires, while in the mutant Collect can succeed immediately, causing a difference in the state balances.

After any sequence of calls to Put and a subsequent call to Collect that succeeds without reverting, the caller's unlockTime in the reference is strictly larger than the block timestamp when the first Put had a positive lockTime, while in the mutant unlockTime is never updated (remains 0), so the reference ensures Collect cannot succeed immediately after Put with a future lockTime, but the mutant allows it, causing the caller's balance after Collect to be less than the total Put amount in the reference but not in the mutant.

After a successful Collect call, the caller's recorded balance in the Acc mapping is exactly equal to the sum of all previous Put amounts minus the collected amount, but because the reference requires the unlock time to be exceeded, the Collect call will revert if the lock time hasn't passed, while the mutant allows Collect immediately, causing a difference in whether Collect succeeds (and thus the balance changes) — so the rule is that after a Put with lockTime > 0 and then a Collect with an amount less than the balance, the Collect succeeds in the mutant but reverts in the reference when the current time is earlier than the unlock time.
After any sequence of calls, the unlockTime of a caller is always equal to the maximum of all timestamp+lockTime from Put calls, unless no Put was ever made, in which case it is 0.
After a Put with a future lockTime, a subsequent Collect of the entire balance succeeds in the mutant but reverts in the reference when block.timestamp is before unlockTime.
After a Collect call, the unlockTime of the caller is at most block.timestamp + _lockTime (when the caller's balance is >= MinSum and >= _am and block.timestamp > unlockTime).
After a Collect call that succeeds, the unlockTime of the caller is less than or equal to block.timestamp + _lockTime.
After a successful Collect call, the caller's unlockTime is exactly block.timestamp + _lockTime (where _lockTime is the parameter of the preceding Put call that set it).

After a successful Collect call, the caller's balance is unchanged if the caller had no prior balance and performed a Put with a given _lockTime, then the Collect fails because block.timestamp is not greater than the unlockTime (due to the +1 bug) — the rule is that the caller's balance after Collect equals the amount they put, but the buggy contract increments unlockTime by one, causing Collect to succeed later and the balance to be reduced, so the rule fails.
After a successful Collect call, the caller's unlockTime is equal to block.timestamp + _lockTime (where _lockTime was the parameter of the preceding Put call that set the unlockTime).
After Collect, the state variable MinSum remains unchanged.

After Collect, the contract's balance minus the sum of all account balances (which is zero because balances are not publicly aggregated) is unchanged, but the actual rule is that the contract's ether balance is unchanged by Collect, which the reference satisfies for all inputs but the buggy version breaks because it reverts when msg.value is zero.
After Collect, the contract's ether balance is unchanged (no net transfer of ether from the contract to the caller).
When Collect is called with a positive amount, the caller's balance in Acc mapping is decreased by that amount (i.e., the contract's recorded balance for the caller is reduced by _am).
After Collect, the sum of the caller's balance in Acc mapping and the contract's ether balance is invariant (stays the same as before the call).
Collect should only succeed when acc.balance >= MinSum, acc.balance >= _am, and block.timestamp > acc.unlockTime
After a Collect call, the sender's balance decreases by exactly _am when the call succeeds (does not revert).
After a Collect call revert, the caller's balance in Acc remains unchanged (since no transfer occurs).
After Collect reverts, the mapping Acc[caller].balance must equal its value before the call.
After Collect reverts, the caller's balance in Acc remains unchanged.
After a call to Collect(am), the caller's balance in the contract is non-negative and does not exceed its previous value.
The condition for withdrawal uses strict inequality (block.timestamp > acc.unlockTime) rather than non-strict inequality (block.timestamp >= acc.unlockTime).

If the caller's balance is exactly equal to the contract's minimum sum, then after a Collect call with amount equal to that balance, the caller's balance in the contract decreases by exactly the withdrawal amount only when the timelock is strictly passed.

If the caller's balance equals the minimum sum and the withdrawal amount equals that balance, a Collect call succeeds only when block.timestamp > acc.unlockTime, not when block.timestamp == acc.unlockTime.
After a successful Collect withdrawal exactly at unlockTime, the caller's balance in the contract remains unchanged (strict inequality check prevents withdrawal at exact unlockTime).
